classification.difficultyReason: Read horizontal and vertical extents from supplied graphs, including closed endpoints and attained extrema while excluding asymptotic bounds. The varied curves require direct graphical interpretation without algebraic derivation or an unsignposted connection.

content.prompt: State the domain and range of the following graphs.

spec.description: Increasing straight line with both ends arrowed; no numerical ticks.
spec.mathematics: Unbounded horizontal and vertical extents; intercepts are not numerically specified.

answer.worked: The line extends indefinitely to the left and right, and down and up. Therefore D: $x\in\mathbb R$ and R: $y\in\mathbb R$.

spec.description: Upward parabola with vertex at the origin and arrowed ends.
spec.mathematics: Minimum ordinate zero; horizontal extent unrestricted. Plot scale is schematic and adds no labelled values.

answer.worked: The parabola extends indefinitely left and right. Its minimum is $y=0$, which is included. Therefore D: $x\in\mathbb R$ and R: $y\ge0$.

spec.description: Increasing cubic-shaped curve through the origin, flat there, with arrowed ends.
spec.mathematics: Both coordinate extents unrestricted; no numerical scale is supplied.

answer.worked: The curve continues indefinitely left and right, and down and up. Therefore D: $x\in\mathbb R$ and R: $y\in\mathbb R$.

spec.description: Upward parabola; dashed guides identify vertex (3,1).
spec.mathematics: Vertex (3,1), minimum y=1; curvature schematic because no equation is supplied.

answer.worked: The parabola extends indefinitely left and right. The vertex $(3,1)$ gives the included minimum $y=1$. Therefore D: $x\in\mathbb R$ and R: $y\ge1$.

spec.description: Cubic-shaped curve through the origin with an upper-left turning point and lower-right turning point.
spec.mathematics: Unbounded in both coordinate directions; unlabelled turning points are schematic.

answer.worked: The turning points do not bound the whole curve: its ends continue down to the left and up to the right. Therefore D: $x\in\mathbb R$ and R: $y\in\mathbb R$.

spec.description: Complete circle centred at the origin with axis intercepts ±2.
spec.mathematics: Circle radius 2; all extreme points included.

answer.worked: The circle reaches $x=-2$ and $x=2$, and $y=-2$ and $y=2$. All four extremes belong to the circle. Therefore D: $-2\le x\le2$ and R: $-2\le y\le2$.

spec.description: Sinusoidal curve with closed endpoints at (−2π,0) and (2π,0), two peaks and two troughs.

answer.worked: The filled endpoints include $x=-2\pi$ and $x=2\pi$. The curve attains its highest value $1$ and lowest value $-1$. Therefore D: $-2\pi\le x\le2\pi$ and R: $-1\le y\le1$.

spec.description: Increasing exponential-shaped curve above the x-axis with arrowed ends.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal asymptote y=0 approached from above; no numerical y-intercept supplied.

answer.worked: The curve extends across every real $x$-value. It stays above the $x$-axis and approaches $y=0$ without reaching it. Therefore D: $x\in\mathbb R$ and R: $y>0$.

spec.description: Decreasing curve through the origin; dashed horizontal asymptote y=1.
spec.mathematics: All real x; all y below 1; curve shape schematic.

answer.worked: The curve extends across every real $x$-value. It approaches $y=1$ from below without reaching it and continues down indefinitely. Therefore D: $x\in\mathbb R$ and R: $y<1$.

spec.description: Right-opening parabola with vertex at the origin and both branches arrowed.
spec.mathematics: All nonnegative x; all real y; curvature schematic.

answer.worked: The leftmost point is the origin, so $x=0$ is included and the curve extends right indefinitely. The two branches extend up and down indefinitely. Therefore D: $x\ge0$ and R: $y\in\mathbb R$.

spec.description: Increasing logarithmic-shaped curve to the right of the y-axis; no numerical intercept.
spec.mathematics: Vertical asymptote x=0; all real y; horizontal scale schematic.

answer.worked: The curve stays to the right of the $y$-axis and approaches it without reaching $x=0$. Its vertical extent is unrestricted. Therefore D: $x>0$ and R: $y\in\mathbb R$.

spec.description: Square-root-shaped curve beginning at the origin and continuing into the first quadrant.
spec.mathematics: Origin included; nonnegative horizontal and vertical extents; no numerical scale.

answer.worked: The curve includes the origin and extends right and up indefinitely. Therefore D: $x\ge0$ and R: $y\ge0$.

spec.description: Upper semicircle of radius 3 with filled endpoints.

answer.worked: The filled endpoints include the horizontal extremes $-3$ and $3$. The semicircle includes its lowest value $0$ and highest value $3$. Therefore D: $-3\le x\le3$ and R: $0\le y\le3$.

spec.description: Complete ellipse centred at the origin, horizontal intercepts ±3 and vertical intercepts ±2.

answer.worked: The ellipse includes its leftmost and rightmost points at $x=-3$ and $x=3$, and its lowest and highest points at $y=-2$ and $y=2$. Therefore D: $-3\le x\le3$ and R: $-2\le y\le2$.

spec.description: Complete circle centred at (2,1), touching the y-axis; guides at y=3 and y=−1.
spec.mathematics: Radius 2; horizontal extremes 0 and 4, vertical extremes −1 and 3.

answer.worked: The circle includes the horizontal extremes $x=0$ and $x=4$, and the vertical extremes $y=-1$ and $y=3$. Therefore D: $0\le x\le4$ and R: $-1\le y\le3$.
